Tyres: Your Only Contact with the Road

Your tyres are the single most important safety component on your motorcycle. Two small contact patches, each roughly the size of a credit card, are all that connect you to the road surface. For UK touring, where wet roads are the norm rather than the exception, choosing the right tyres is critical for confidence, safety, and enjoyment.

Touring Tyre Characteristics

Touring tyres differ from sport tyres in several important ways:

  • Longevity — Harder compounds last 8,000-12,000 miles compared to 3,000-5,000 for sport tyres. Essential when you are covering hundreds of miles daily.
  • Wet grip — Deep tread patterns channel water efficiently. UK touring demands tyres that inspire confidence on wet roads.
  • Stability under load — Touring tyres have stiffer carcasses that maintain their profile under the weight of luggage and rider.
  • Comfort — Touring compounds absorb road imperfections better than rock-hard sport compounds, reducing fatigue.

Best Touring Tyres 2026

Michelin Road 6 — The benchmark touring tyre. Exceptional wet grip from Michelin's silica-rich compound, long life, and surprisingly good feel when pushing on through bends. The tyre most touring riders choose for good reason.

Bridgestone T32 — The Battlax T32 offers outstanding wet performance rivalling the Michelin. Slightly more sporting feel and excellent feedback through corners. Wears well with balanced front-to-rear life.

Continental ContiRoadAttack 4 — Excellent all-round touring tyre with Continental's TractionSkin technology for good grip on new tyres. Long life and consistent performance throughout the tyre's lifespan.

Metzeler Roadtec 02 — A dual-compound tyre with harder centre for longevity and softer edges for cornering grip. The Interact technology adapts to rider inputs for a confident feel in all conditions.

Pirelli Angel GT II — Sporty touring tyre that offers the best dry grip in the touring category while maintaining respectable wet performance and reasonable tyre life.

Never compromise on tyres. They are the most important safety purchase you make for your motorcycle. A premium touring tyre costs roughly twenty to thirty pounds more than a budget option but delivers dramatically better grip, especially in the wet British conditions we ride in most often.

When to Replace

Replace touring tyres when tread depth reaches 2mm. The legal minimum is 1mm but grip deteriorates significantly below 2mm, especially in wet conditions. Inspect tyres for cracks, bulges, and uneven wear before every tour. Age also matters — replace tyres over five years old regardless of remaining tread.

Touring compounds last 8,000-12,000 miles versus 3,000-5,000 for sport tyres.
The Michelin Road 6 is the benchmark for wet grip and longevity.

Replace tyres over five years old regardless of remaining tread.

Deep tread and silica compounds inspire wet confidence.

cons: Premium tyres cost a little more than budget options.

faq.q: How long do touring tyres last?
faq.a: Touring tyres use harder compounds that last 8,000-12,000 miles, compared with 3,000-5,000 for sport tyres, which is essential when covering hundreds of miles daily. They also feature deep tread patterns for wet grip and stiffer carcasses that hold their profile under luggage and rider weight.

faq.q: Which touring tyre should I buy?
faq.a: The Michelin Road 6 is the benchmark, offering exceptional wet grip from a silica-rich compound, long life and good feel when pushing on. The Bridgestone T32 rivals it with a slightly sportier feel, while the Metzeler Roadtec 02 uses a dual compound for longevity and cornering grip.

faq.q: When should I replace touring tyres?
faq.a: Replace them when tread depth reaches 2mm. The legal minimum is 1mm, but grip deteriorates significantly below 2mm, especially in the wet British conditions we ride in most. Inspect for cracks, bulges and uneven wear before every tour, and replace any tyre over five years old regardless of tread.

faq.q: Is it worth paying for premium tyres?
faq.a: Yes. A premium touring tyre costs roughly twenty to thirty pounds more than a budget option but delivers dramatically better grip, especially in the wet. Tyres are the most important safety purchase for your motorcycle, so they are never the place to economise on a touring machine.
